newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Oklahoma harvest winding down.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Oklahoma harvest winding down.

text.p: Harvesting of hard red winter wheat in Oklahoma was winding down, grain dealers said Thursday.
"Things are starting to slow down. Some parts of northern Oklahoma's still taking in a lot of wheat, but by and large we're almost done," a north central Oklahoma dealer said.

Meanwhile, dealers in northern Kansas said they were trying to cope with the problems caused by abundant supplies of wheat and a shortage of trucks and railcars. Many elevators were forced to pile wheat on the ground for lack of a better alternative.
"We've got so much wheat on the ground up here -- there's not enough trucks, not enough railcars and not enough concrete," a north central Kansas dealer said.
Showers overnight in northern Kansas and southern Nebraska will likely cause some disruption to harvesting Thursday as combine operators wait for fields to dry.
Dealers speculated they could soon see an increase in farmer selling in northern Oklahoma and southern Kansas as the 30-day free storage period expires.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
